answer.rationale: The two live symptoms (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel itself, not at price. Promotional pricing is the tempting answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 explicitly ties deep discounts to renewal risk and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so trading renewal quality for a signup spike is the wrong bet with a single non-carryover slot. Referral incentive and enterprise sales assist are both plausible but neither addresses the observed regression. That leaves the onboarding/activation cluster. I want the two memories that would actually carry the chosen action: memory_31 (signup field reduction, SMB activation) and memory_86 (onboarding shortening, completion and time-to-value) — these are the direct evidentiary basis for simplify_onboarding, and both are old (day 12 and day 52) consolidations whose original records I have not seen. Key things verification must settle: whether memory_31's 'durable lift' was measured beyond week one, whether memory_86's completion lift came with any effect on account quality, and whether either was measured in a segment resembling today's price-pressured SMB mix. Downstream risk flagged because cutting required signup fields can raise raw activation while degrading lead qualification data and thus downstream qualified revenue — the exact metric I am optimizing — so success criteria must include a quality-of-account measure, not completion rate alone. If verification shows memory_31's lift was short-horizon only or measured in a non-comparable segment, I would shift the slot to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger 6% decline. Standard experiment scale with a quality guardrail rather than broad rollout, since the causes of both declines are still unexplained and could be competitor-driven mix shift rather than funnel friction.
